router_body:
name: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: full job set selected
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: echo 'SELECTED test nvim-plugin vscode-extension vscode-package server-lane helix-config zed-extension emacs-mode independence tier'
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
      - name: local gate wiring proof
        if: ${{ github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix') }}
        run: python3 -I ci/local-gate-test.py
      - name: local evidence gate
        if: ${{ !(github.event_name != 'pull_request' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'full-matrix') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release-matrix')) }}
        run: echo 'Local gauntlet evidence is the gate; request ci or full-matrix for CI.'

ci.yml.test:
name: test (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'test')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all and full tiers (on macOS the merge's smoke, tl30),
        # ubuntu alone in a pull request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_test || '[]') }}
    steps:
      # No `submodules:` key, deliberately. `upstream/` is the private wolf-lang
      # repo and org policy disables deploy keys, so CI cannot clone it at all;
      # the tracked `vendor/upstream` snapshot is the CI path (vendor/README.md).
      # The gitlink pin stays visible via `git submodule status --cached`.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # The runner image ships some toolchain; `rust-toolchain.toml` names the
      # one we test against. Install it explicitly — an implicit rustup
      # proxy-install races the first cargo invocation and picks up neither
      # rustfmt nor clippy.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: |
          rustup show active-toolchain
          rustup component add rustfmt clippy

      - name: Toolchain versions
        run: |
          rustc --version
          cargo --version
          cargo fmt --version
          cargo clippy --version

      - name: rustfmt
        run: cargo fmt --all --check

      - name: clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: test
        run: cargo test --workspace

      # PIN well-formed always; snapshot == submodule only where the submodule
      # exists, which in CI is never.
      - name: sync-pin
        run: cargo xtask sync-pin

      # The one local `.lu` exists only because a recorded gap says it may.
      - name: fixtures-check
        run: cargo xtask fixtures-check

      # The Neovim plugin's derived artifacts still agree with the pin: the
      # 50-keyword set in `syntax/wolf.vim` against `grammar.ebnf`'s
      # `reserved_kw`, and the generated `lua/wolf/pin.lua` against `PIN`. This
      # is the drift check ls04 §2 owes. It covers keywords only — the vendored
      # EBNF elides the operator precedence climb, and the command's own
      # documentation says so rather than implying wider coverage.
      - name: nvim-check (derived artifacts)
        run: cargo xtask nvim-check

      # The VS Code extension's four GENERATED files still agree with the pin:
      # the three `.tmLanguage.json` grammars and `src/pin.ts`. Unlike
      # `nvim-check`, which compares a keyword list inside a human-written
      # file, this regenerates each artifact and compares BYTES — a
      # `.tmLanguage.json` is two hundred lines of escaped regex, and a
      # hand-edit in the middle of one is invisible to any check that only
      # inspects the terminal lists (ls05 §2).
      #
      # Covers keywords AND the operator inventory, and covers neither more
      # than it can: the vendored EBNF elides the precedence climb, so
      # thirteen operators are absent from the derivation entirely. The
      # command's own documentation says so, and a unit test fails the day
      # upstream closes the gap.
      - name: grammar-drift (VS Code derived artifacts)
        run: cargo xtask grammar-drift

      # ls06's two editor-free gates. `config-check` is the only thing that
      # reads all four config-tier clients at once, and the invariants it holds
      # are exactly the ones no single editor can check: that every client
      # spawns `wolf lsp` and nothing else (D34), that `.wolfi` is attached to
      # no server anywhere, that no editor references the empty
      # `tree-sitter-wolf`, and that the formatter's two numbers are the same
      # numbers in all of them.
      - name: config-check (helix + zed + the shared numbers)
        run: cargo xtask config-check

      # The emacs keyword drift gate, in Rust rather than elisp so that it runs
      # on a machine with no Emacs — the `emacs-mode` job below needs the editor
      # and this must not depend on that job being green.
      - name: emacs-check (derived keyword list)
        run: cargo xtask emacs-check

      # Transcripts and their scripts: parseable, valid, canonical, and each
      # transcript still has the script that regenerates it.
      - name: lspconf verify (server-free)
        run: cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- verify

      # Capability profiles, plus the loud list of clients nobody has read yet.
      - name: lspconf profiles (server-free)
        run: cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- profiles

  # The Neovim plugin, loaded by a real Neovim, on the full D35 tier-1 host set
  # (ls04 acceptance). This lane needs NO `wolf` binary: everything it asserts —
  # filetypes, buffer options, syntax groups, commands, config resolution,
  # root-marker priority, tree-sitter absence, the quickfix conversion and the
  # whole `:checkhealth wolf` report — is true of a machine with no toolchain,
  # which is the state every runner here is in. That is what makes the plugin
  # lane the one editor lane that is NOT dark.
  #
  # It is a separate job from `test` on purpose: `cargo test --workspace` there
  # runs the same file and SKIPS it (no editor on those runners), which is
  # correct for a developer's laptop and useless as a gate. Here the editor's
  # presence is checked first and its absence is a hard failure.
ci.yml.nvim-plugin:
name: nvim plugin (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'nvim-plugin')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all tier (the nightly), ubuntu and windows in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap), ubuntu alone in a pull
        # request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_nvim_plugin || '[]') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      # Neovim from its own release assets rather than from three different
      # package managers, so all three runners agree on a version.
      #
      # `stable` is a real tag in `neovim/neovim` that always points at the
      # latest stable release; the plugin's floor is 0.11 and `:checkhealth`
      # enforces it, so tracking stable is the honest choice — a plugin whose
      # CI pins an old editor stops noticing the day the editor changes.
      #
      # These asset NAMES have churned historically (the linux tarball was
      # `nvim-linux64.tar.gz` before 0.11). A rename therefore fails this step
      # loudly, which is the intended behaviour: silently falling back to a
      # system Neovim would test a different editor than the one named here.
      - name: Install Neovim (linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o nvim.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/stable/nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
          tar xzf nvim.tar.gz
          echo "$PWD/nvim-linux-x86_64/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install Neovim (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o nvim.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/stable/nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz
          # The macOS tarballs are notarised; extended attributes on the
          # extracted tree make Gatekeeper refuse the binary on some runners.
          xattr -c nvim.tar.gz || true
          tar xzf nvim.tar.gz
          echo "$PWD/nvim-macos-arm64/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install Neovim (windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri `
            'https://github.com/neovim/neovim/releases/download/stable/nvim-win64.zip' `
            -OutFile nvim.zip
          Expand-Archive -Path nvim.zip -DestinationPath .
          "$PWD\nvim-win64\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      # Presence is the gate. `cargo test --test nvim_plugin` skips politely
      # when there is no editor, and a job whose whole purpose is the editor
      # must not be allowed to take that exit.
      - name: Neovim version (the floor is 0.11)
        shell: bash
        run: nvim --version

      - name: The plugin lane
        shell: bash
        run: cargo test --test nvim_plugin -- --nocapture

  # The VS Code extension, loaded by a real headless VS Code, on the full D35
  # tier-1 host set (ls05 acceptance). Like the Neovim lane, this needs NO
  # `wolf` binary for its first half: contributions, activation, language
  # registration, the settings surface, the command set and the absence of
  # semantic-token UI are all true of a machine with no toolchain. The server
  # half inside the suite reports SKIP with a reason when there is none.
  #
  # It is a separate job from `test` on purpose, and for a sharper reason than
  # the Neovim lane has. `cargo test --test vscode_extension` runs the GRAMMAR
  # lane and deliberately stops there: `@vscode/test-electron` *downloads* a VS
  # Code build on first use, and a `cargo test` that silently starts a 150 MB
  # download is a `cargo test` people stop running. Here the download is the
  # job's whole point, so it is explicit.
ci.yml.vscode-extension:
# ubuntu only: the darwin-arm64 @vscode/test-electron download spawns
    # ENOENT on the hosted runner (never had a green run — README caveat
    # was accurate); mac/windows verification is local-only until someone
    # owns that investigation. Honest matrix over aspirational matrix.
    name: vscode extension (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'vscode-extension')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The host is the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, in every tier.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_vscode_extension || '[]') }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: clients/vscode
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: clients/vscode/package-lock.json

      # `ci`, never `install`: the lock file is committed precisely so that a
      # CI run and a laptop resolve the same tree. `npm install` is allowed to
      # rewrite it, which makes the lock file advisory and the lane unpinned.
      - name: Install (locked)
        run: npm ci

      - name: Toolchain versions
        run: |
          node --version
          npm --version

      - name: Compile
        run: npm run compile

      # No VS Code needed, no display needed. Runs first because a broken
      # grammar should not be reported as a failure to launch an editor.
      - name: Grammar lane (tokenizer + reviewed scope snapshots)
        run: npm run test:grammar

      # wolf-lsp#47: the suite's server half needs `wolf` at the pin, and this
      # job never had one, so the half skipped on every run. The acquisition
      # is the one every server job uses (`.github/actions/acquire-wolf`, the
      # pin's own tag, `.wolf-bin/` at the workspace root: a composite
      # action's steps do not take this job's `working-directory`). The
      # binary reaches the suite as `WOLF_BIN`, which `runTest.ts` puts on the
      # test window's `PATH` as a directory, the discovery path a user has.
      - name: Acquire the wolf binary at the pin
        id: acquire
        uses: ./.github/actions/acquire-wolf

      # Headless VS Code. On linux `runTest.ts` passes
      # `--ozone-platform=headless` (wolf-lsp#48), so the lane needs no virtual
      # display, and none is given: `DISPLAY` and `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` are unset on
      # purpose, so a regression back to needing one is red here instead of
      # being papered over by `xvfb-run`. macOS and windows runners have a
      # display.
      #
      # `WOLF_REQUIRE_SERVER=1` (wolf-lsp#47): the suite's server half FAILS
      # where it used to skip, so this job cannot be green while that half is
      # dark. It skipped on every run before this, `no \`wolf\` on PATH in the
      # test window`, and nothing noticed.
      - name: Extension lane (headless VS Code, linux, no display)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        env:
          WOLF_REQUIRE_SERVER: '1'
          WOLF_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/.wolf-bin/wolf
        run: env -u DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY npm run test:extension

      - name: Extension lane (headless VS Code, macOS and windows)
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        env:
          WOLF_REQUIRE_SERVER: '1'
          WOLF_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/.wolf-bin/wolf
        run: npm run test:extension

      # The install path `clients/vscode/README.md` documents, run as CI so the
      # instructions cannot rot (ls05 §3 acceptance: "the install commands in
      # the README are the ones CI runs"). The size budget is a gate, not a
      # note: the vsix is 316 KB today and the ceiling exists so that a
      # dependency that quietly ships megabytes fails here rather than in a
      # user's download.
      - name: Package the vsix
        run: npm run package

      - name: The vsix is under budget
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bytes=$(wc -c < wolf-0.0.1.vsix)
          echo "wolf-0.0.1.vsix: $bytes bytes"
          if [ "$bytes" -gt 1048576 ]; then
            echo "::error::the vsix is $bytes bytes, over the 1 MiB budget."
            echo "::error::check .vscodeignore and the runtime dependency set."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Installs into a THROWAWAY profile, then asks the editor to list what it
      # has. Installing and *being installed* are different claims, and only
      # the second one is what a user gets.
      - name: Install the vsix into a throwaway profile
        run: npm run install:vsix

  # The publish DRY RUN, and the artifact it would have uploaded (ls07 §1).
  #
  # ==========================================================================
  # THIS JOB PUBLISHES NOTHING, HOLDS NO SECRET, AND CANNOT REACH A REGISTRY.
  # ==========================================================================
  #
  # `@vscode/vsce` has no `--dry-run`, so the rehearsal is assembled from the
  # three things that run offline and together cover everything `vsce publish`
  # checks before it opens a socket: `vsce package` (same manifest validation,
  # same prepublish script, same file selection), `vsce ls` compared against a
  # REVIEWED contents list, and a manifest lint for the listing fields `vsce`
  # does not enforce. What is left after all three is the upload — and the
  # upload is human-gated on a publisher identity this repository must never
  # hold (docs/DISTRIBUTION.md §"OWED TO HUMAN").
  #
  # Separate from `vscode-extension` on purpose, and the split is not
  # duplication: that job downloads a 150 MB VS Code to answer "does the
  # extension load and install", and this one answers "is the artifact a
  # publish would upload the artifact somebody reviewed" — in about a minute,
  # with no editor. Keeping them apart means the packaging gate stays green and
  # fast on a day the editor download is broken, which has already happened
  # once on macOS runners.
ci.yml.vscode-package:
name: vscode package (publish dry run)
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'vscode-package')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: clients/vscode
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: clients/vscode/package-lock.json

      - name: Install (locked)
        run: npm ci

      - name: Compile
        run: npm run compile

      # `vsce ls` against PACKAGE-CONTENTS.txt, plus the listing-field lint.
      # Fails on a `.vscodeignore` change or a new runtime dependency, so what
      # ships to a user is a reviewed diff rather than a surprise.
      - name: The publish dry run (contents + manifest lint)
        run: npm run test:manifest

      - name: Package the vsix
        run: npm run package

      - name: The vsix is under budget
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bytes=$(wc -c < wolf-0.0.1.vsix)
          echo "wolf-0.0.1.vsix: $bytes bytes"
          if [ "$bytes" -gt 1048576 ]; then
            echo "::error::the vsix is $bytes bytes, over the 1 MiB budget."
            echo "::error::check .vscodeignore and the runtime dependency set."
            exit 1
          fi

      # The per-run artifact, which is the only "distribution" this repository
      # performs: a build somebody can download from the run that produced it,
      # traceable to a commit, expiring on its own. It is NOT a release channel
      # and the retention is short so nobody mistakes it for one.
      - name: Keep the vsix as a per-run artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: wolf-vsix-${{ github.sha }}
          path: clients/vscode/*.vsix
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  # Does a server exist at the pin? Report it, on every platform — and FAIL
  # when the answer is no, because at a released pin "no" means this file asked
  # the wrong question. The old posture ("never fail the build for its
  # absence") was written when wolf-lang published nothing at all; it outlived
  # that, and wolf-lsp#28 is what it cost. The one surviving green-while-dark
  # path is an unreleased (trunk) pin, and it announces itself.
ci.yml.server-lane:
name: server lane (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'server-lane')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all tier (the nightly), ubuntu and windows in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap), ubuntu alone in a pull
        # request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_server_lane || '[]') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      # ACQUISITION lives in `.github/actions/acquire-wolf` — one copy, shared
      # with `nightly.yml`, because wolf-lsp#28 (b) is the cost of two copies:
      # this file grew an acquisition and the nightly never did, so its sweep
      # and latency jobs had no subject and reported success for every night
      # this repository has existed.
      #
      # What it must NEVER become: a `cargo build` of the compiler. The
      # interpreter track paid for that lesson (private submodule, no deploy
      # keys), and a multi-minute compiler build per job to produce a binary we
      # are supposed to download is the wrong shape regardless. The local
      # instructions live in the README, where a human can follow them once.
      #
      # ITS HISTORY, kept because both halves were wrong at some point:
      #   * ls00..wolf-lsp#3 asked for `wolf-<shortsha>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, a
      #     name `xtask dist` has never published — it writes
      #     `wolf-<version>-<triple>.tar.gz` — and it named linux in the
      #     pattern while running a three-OS matrix, so two thirds of the
      #     matrix could only ever report SERVER UNAVAILABLE.
      #   * wolf-lsp#28 (a): it then asked the LATEST release for the PIN's
      #     asset, which matches only while pin and latest agree.
      - name: Acquire the wolf binary at the pin
        id: acquire
        uses: ./.github/actions/acquire-wolf

      # `doctor` is the authority, not the acquisition step: it re-resolves the
      # binary, compares `--version` against PIN, and prints the verdict. Exit
      # 77 is "skipped", which is a success here and a failure under
      # --require-server.
      - name: lspconf doctor
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          set +e   # shell: bash wraps with -e; exit 77 is data here, not death
          out=$(cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- doctor 2>&1)
          rc=$?
          printf '%s\n' "$out"
          printf '%s\n' "$out" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          # 77 is "no binary". After a SUCCESSFUL download that is not a skip,
          # it is an extraction or a locate bug — the acquisition said it put a
          # server on disk and doctor cannot find one. Only the unreleased-pin
          # path above reaches this branch legitimately.
          case "$rc" in
            0)  echo "server READY at the pin" ;;
            77) if [ "${{ steps.acquire.outputs.server }}" = "downloaded" ]; then
                  echo "::error::acquisition reported a download, doctor finds no binary"
                  exit 1
                fi
                echo "::notice::server lane skipped — PIN is at an unreleased wolf" ;;
            *)  echo "::error::doctor failed with $rc"; exit "$rc" ;;
          esac

      # THE SERVER LANE PROPER. These RUN here, on all three OSes, whenever the
      # pin names a released wolf — which is every pin this repo has ever
      # carried. `--require-server` turns a skip into a failure, which is how a
      # job that believes it has a binary proves it had one. The `if` below is
      # not a convenience: it is reachable only on the unreleased-pin path,
      # because every other absence failed the acquisition outright.
      # wolf-lsp#24: the builtin TYPE list against the compiler. Every name
      # in TYPE_NAMES and TYPE_POSITION_UNPAINTED must resolve in type
      # position at the pin, and every `type.<name>` anchor in the vendored
      # spec index that resolves must be in one of the two lists. The oracle
      # is the acquired binary, so this runs only where one resolved.
      - name: type-names-check (server-dependent)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server == 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        run: cargo xtask type-names-check --require-server

      - name: Conformance replay (server-dependent)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server == 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        run: cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- --require-server replay

      - name: One truth — publishDiagnostics == conform-run (D34)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server == 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        run: cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- --require-server onetruth

      # The server-gated suites. They are part of `cargo test --workspace` in
      # the job above too, where they skip; naming them here is what makes the
      # difference between "skipped" and "ran" visible in the log.
      - name: Encoding, negotiation, semantics, oracle and stability suites
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server == 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cargo test --test negotiation --test encoding --test semantics \
                     --test fuzz_oracles --test stability --test one_truth \
                     --test teardown

      # 60 s of seeded fuzzing on a PR; the 15-minute sweep is nightly (s01/s02
      # posture). The seed is explicit and constant so a failure here is
      # reproducible on a laptop with one command.
      - name: Fuzzed partial-edit session (seeded, bounded)
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server == 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        timeout-minutes: 3
        run: cargo run --quiet --bin lspconf -- --require-server fuzz regions.lu --seed 1 --splices 64

      # Reachable ONLY at an unreleased (trunk) pin — every other absence is a
      # failed acquisition, not a skip. It stays loud anyway: this is the one
      # green-while-dark path left in this workflow, and a reader of the run
      # should not have to infer it from a job that finished suspiciously fast.
      - name: Report the skip
        if: steps.acquire.outputs.server != 'downloaded'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          echo "::warning::server lane dark at an UNRELEASED pin ${{ steps.acquire.outputs.pin }}"
          echo "SKIP: PIN names wolf ${{ steps.acquire.outputs.version }}, which is not a release tag"
          echo "SKIP: replay, onetruth, type-names, encoding, semantics, oracles and fuzz are dark HERE"
          echo "SKIP: re-pin to a released tag to light them; they run green locally, see README."
          {
            echo "### Server lane: SKIPPED (unreleased pin)"
            echo "\`PIN\` names wolf \`${{ steps.acquire.outputs.version }}\` at"
            echo "\`${{ steps.acquire.outputs.pin }}\`, whose version string carries build"
            echo "metadata, so wolf-lang publishes no archive to acquire."
            echo ""
            echo "\`wolf lsp\` **exists** at this pin — wolf-lang s52 shipped it and"
            echo "\`PIN\` records \`serves_lsp = true\`. This repo does not build the compiler"
            echo "in CI (\`vendor/README.md\`). Replay, one-truth, the encoding and semantics"
            echo "suites, the fuzz oracles and the latency budgets all run green against a"
            echo "locally-built binary — see \`README.md\`, *Running the server lane locally*."
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ls06, the config tier. Three jobs rather than one, so a red row in
  # docs/MATRIX.md names exactly one job and one editor.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # Helix (T2). The whole value of this lane is that HELIX does the parsing:
  # `cargo xtask helix-health` drops `clients/helix/languages.toml` into a temp
  # config dir and reads `hx --health` back.
  #
  # Two behaviours shape it, both verified rather than assumed:
  #   * `hx --health` ALWAYS exits 0 — unknown language, missing server,
  #     unparseable fragment, all zero — so the assertion is entirely on stdout;
  #   * it prints `Tree-sitter parser: ✓` for a grammar that does not exist, so
  #     the check reads the `Highlight queries:` line and ignores the other.
  #
  # The command SKIPS with exit 77 when it cannot prove helix loaded our
  # fragment, so a platform whose config directory is not `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`
  # reports a skip instead of passing vacuously. windows is in the matrix for
  # exactly that reason: the skip is the information.
ci.yml.helix-config:
name: helix config (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'helix-config')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all tier (the nightly), ubuntu and windows in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap), ubuntu alone in a pull
        # request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_helix_config || '[]') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      # From the release assets rather than three package managers, for the
      # same reason the Neovim lane does it: all three runners agree on a
      # version, and an asset rename fails loudly instead of silently falling
      # back to a system helix that is a different editor than the one named.
      - name: Install helix (linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o hx.tar.xz \
            https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/releases/download/25.07.1/helix-25.07.1-x86_64-linux.tar.xz
          tar xJf hx.tar.xz
          echo "$PWD/helix-25.07.1-x86_64-linux" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install helix (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -fsSL -o hx.tar.xz \
            https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/releases/download/25.07.1/helix-25.07.1-aarch64-macos.tar.xz
          xattr -c hx.tar.xz || true
          tar xJf hx.tar.xz
          echo "$PWD/helix-25.07.1-aarch64-macos" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Install helix (windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri `
            'https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/releases/download/25.07.1/helix-25.07.1-x86_64-windows.zip' `
            -OutFile hx.zip
          Expand-Archive -Path hx.zip -DestinationPath .
          "$PWD\helix-25.07.1-x86_64-windows" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      - name: helix version
        shell: bash
        run: hx --version

      # Exit 77 is a SKIP with a reason, not a pass and not a death — the same
      # contract `lspconf doctor` uses (ls00 §3). It is surfaced in the job
      # summary so a dark lane is a lane somebody notices is dark.
      - name: hx --health against the shipped fragment
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set +e
          out=$(cargo run --quiet -p xtask -- helix-health 2>&1)
          code=$?
          echo "$out"
          if [ "$code" = "77" ]; then
            {
              echo "### helix lane: SKIPPED on ${{ matrix.os }}"
              echo ""
              echo '```'
              echo "$out"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          exit "$code"

  # Zed (T2). CI BUILDS the wasm; CI does NOT run Zed. That asymmetry is the
  # honest state of this row and it is recorded in docs/MATRIX.md rather than
  # hidden: Zed's dev-extension install is a GUI action (`zed::InstallDevExtension`)
  # with no CLI flag and no settings.json equivalent, so there is no headless
  # path in and therefore no recorded session and no capability profile.
  #
  # ubuntu only: the artifact is a `wasm32-wasip2` component and is
  # platform-independent, so building it three times would cost three times as
  # much to prove the same thing.
ci.yml.zed-extension:
name: zed extension (wasm build)
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'zed-extension')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      # `wasm32-wasip2`, not wasip1. Zed's `extension_builder.rs` pins
      # `const RUST_TARGET: &str = "wasm32-wasip2"`; ls06 §2 says wasip1 and is
      # out of date. Delta recorded in the campaign closeout.
      - name: Add the wasm target
        run: rustup target add wasm32-wasip2

      # The host check first: it is fast, and it separates "the API usage is
      # wrong" from "the wasm toolchain is unhappy" — two failures that look
      # identical when only the second command runs.
      - name: Type-check against the host target
        run: cargo check --manifest-path clients/zed/Cargo.toml

      - name: Build the extension component
        run: cargo build --manifest-path clients/zed/Cargo.toml --target wasm32-wasip2 --release

      - name: The component exists and is not empty
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          wasm=clients/zed/target/wasm32-wasip2/release/zed_wolf.wasm
          test -s "$wasm"
          ls -l "$wasm"

  # Emacs (T2). Binary-free: `tests/mode-test.el` asserts the mode, the syntax
  # table, the formatter's numbers, the keyword set and the README/`.el`
  # agreement, none of which needs a `wolf` on PATH — which is what keeps this
  # lane from being dark on a runner (ls00 §3).
  #
  # `tests/server-test.el` is deliberately NOT run here: it needs a `wolf`
  # binary at the pin and would exit 77 on every runner. It runs locally, and
  # the session it records is committed as transcripts/emacs/smoke.jsonl.
ci.yml.emacs-mode:
name: emacs mode (${{ matrix.os }})
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'emacs-mode')
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The hosts are the plan's (ci/tiers.py MATRIX): ubuntu, macOS and
        # windows in the all tier (the nightly), ubuntu and windows in the
        # full tier (the merge; tl30, the macOS cap), ubuntu alone in a pull
        # request's.
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix_emacs_mode || '[]') }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install Emacs (linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends emacs-nox

      - name: Install Emacs (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        run: brew install emacs

      - name: Install Emacs (windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          choco install emacs --no-progress -y
          "C:\Program Files\Emacs\emacs\bin" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_PATH -Encoding utf8 -Append

      # Presence is the gate. eglot has shipped in-tree since Emacs 29, so the
      # floor is 29 and there is no package to install for the LSP half.
      - name: Emacs version (the floor is 29, for bundled eglot)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          emacs --version | head -1
          emacs --batch --eval "(require 'eglot)" --eval "(princ \"eglot is bundled\n\")"

      - name: The mode lane
        shell: bash
        run: |
          emacs --batch -l clients/emacs/tests/mode-test.el \
                -f ert-run-tests-batch-and-exit

  # The editor layer talks to a process, or it does not talk (D34).
ci.yml.independence:
name: independence
    needs: plan
    if: contains(fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.jobs || '[]'), 'independence')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show active-toolchain

      - name: No compiler code, no compiler build, stdio only
        run: cargo xtask independence

      - name: The pin is a recorded revision, not a moving branch
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # Reads the gitlink the superproject records, which works without the
          # submodule being checked out — the only way to verify a pin in a CI
          # job that cannot clone it.
          git submodule status --cached upstream || true
          gitlink=$(git rev-parse HEAD:upstream 2>/dev/null || true)
          if [ -z "$gitlink" ]; then
            echo "::error::no gitlink recorded for upstream/."
            echo "::error::.gitmodules names the submodule but no commit records a sha for it."
            echo "::error::fix: git submodule add https://github.com/wolffe-lang/wolf-lang.git upstream"
            echo "::error::     git -C upstream checkout \$(grep '^commit' vendor/upstream/PIN | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d ' \"')"
            echo "::error::     git add .gitmodules upstream"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "gitlink: $gitlink"

      - name: The vendored PIN agrees with the recorded gitlink
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          gitlink=$(git rev-parse HEAD:upstream 2>/dev/null || true)
          pinned=$(grep '^commit' vendor/upstream/PIN | cut -d= -f2 | tr -d ' "')
          if [ -z "$gitlink" ]; then
            echo "::error::no gitlink for upstream/ — see the previous step"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$gitlink" != "$pinned" ]; then
            echo "::error::PIN says $pinned but the submodule gitlink is $gitlink"
            echo "::error::a pin bump moves both, in one commit (vendor/README.md)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "pin and gitlink agree: $pinned"

      - name: No CRLF reached the working tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          # LSP positions are derived from byte offsets; a CRLF checkout
          # silently shifts every column in every transcript. `.gitattributes`
          # pins `eol=lf`, and this proves it held.
          bad=$(git grep -Il $'\r' -- ':!*.png' ':!*.pdf' || true)
          if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
            echo "::error::CRLF found in: $bad"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "no CRLF in tracked text files"

  # The run's verdict, and its name: `tier full`, `tier pr` or `tier noop`.
  # It needs every job, runs unless the run was cancelled, and fails unless
  # the plan succeeded, the jobs and hosts it chose are the tier's, every
  # chosen job succeeded and every other job was skipped (ci/tiers.py
  # verdict). lane-audit.sh reads this job's name and conclusion.
ci.yml.tier:
name: tier ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tier || 'unplanned' }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
    needs:
      - plan
      - test
      - nvim-plugin
      - vscode-extension
      - vscode-package
      - server-lane
      - helix-config
      - zed-extension
      - emacs-mode
      - independence
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: every chosen job succeeded, every other was skipped
        env:
          NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 ci/tiers.py verdict

  # A red nightly opens an issue (ruling #92): a scheduled run has no lane
  # watching it, so the red has to come and find one. One open issue per
  # workflow, its title the dedupe key; a further red night comments on it
  # (ci/nightly-red.sh, tested by ci/tiers-test.py T8). Never on a pull
  # request, a push or a dispatch: those reds have a lane attached already.
ci.yml.nightly-red:
name: nightly red, an issue
    needs: tier
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: open or update the nightly-red issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
        run: ci/nightly-red.sh
